label: Django + PostgreSQL
summary: Preset: a Django application with its own PostgreSQL database; /admin is internal only.

items: Your content is a git branch or an uploaded package. It is inspected, then goes live within about 2 minutes.
If a new release fails inspection or does not answer, the last good release stays live.
Nothing is built on the server: ship everything the app needs in the release. Put dependencies in `vendor/` (`pip install --target vendor`); it is on `PYTHONPATH`.
PostgreSQL runs on this container on loopback. `os.environ` has `DB_HOST` (`127.0.0.1`), `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DATABASE_URL`.
Your first schema: name a .sql file of your release under Database on the site page. It is loaded once, while the database is empty.
Files your app writes (uploads) must go in data folders, which an installer sets up for your site: they are kept across releases and backed up. Every push replaces the release itself.
The app listens on `127.0.0.1:3000` behind Caddy: the start command is `gunicorn app:app` unless an installer changes it; gunicorn is bound to `$PORT` for you.
`/admin/*` is only reachable from your own networks.
